title: One operator-configurable setting, with its provenance and current mutability
description: Source: src/box/operatorConfig/ (registry.ts for the metadata, precedence.ts for configured/effective/source, policy.ts for mutable/blockers). THE DOMAIN KEY IS THE API, NOT THE ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE: `key` is a stable camelCase name such as `maxBoxCapitalRupees`, and `env_var` is provenance only, shown in an Advanced detail. THREE VALUES ARE DISTINCT AND ALL THREE ARE SENT: `configured_value` is what the operator asked for, `effective_value` is what the engine enforces, and `default_value` is the code default. They diverge when an explicitly-set deployment ceiling clamps an operator value, which is exactly the case `clamped_by_deployment` and `source: runtime_clamped_by_env` exist to make visible — a UI that showed only one number would report a limit that is not in force. `session_snapshot_value` is non-null ONLY for a NEXT_SESSION setting while a session is armed, and carries the value frozen at arm time, so the UI can never present a newly configured ceiling as though the armed session were already using it. NO SECRET IS EVER CARRIED HERE: only environment variables classified as plain `config` in src/env/secrets.ts may be registered, and a backend test asserts it. CLOSED so an added field is caught.

key.description: Stable camelCase domain key. The wire and persisted identity.

label.description: Human label, shown first. Never an environment variable name.

configured_value.description: What the operator has configured: the persisted runtime value if present, else the environment value, else the code default.

effective_value.description: What the engine actually enforces, after deployment containment. May be stricter than configured_value.

source.description: Which layer supplied effective_value. `runtime_clamped_by_env` means an operator value is NOT in force because a deployment bound overrides it.

deployment_bound.description: The absolute bound this deployment set, when the setting is a ceiling/floor and its environment variable was explicitly set. Null means the deployment expressed no opinion.

clamped_by_deployment.description: True when configured_value differs from effective_value because of deployment_bound.

zero_means.description: What 0 means for this setting. `unlimited` matters: for those settings 0 is the LEAST restrictive value, not the most.

safe_direction.description: Which direction of change REDUCES risk. Published because it is NOT derivable from the number: raising minExpectedNetProfit is safer while raising maxOpenBoxes is riskier, and both are 'a bigger number'. The frontend uses this to decide which edits need a dangerous-change confirmation, so that judgement comes from backend metadata rather than a second implementation of the rule that could disagree. Note for a ceiling with zero_means: unlimited, 0 is the LEAST safe value, so direction must be read together with zero_means.

mutable.description: Whether this setting can be changed RIGHT NOW, in the system's current state. False with an empty blockers array is not possible — a refusal always names its reasons.

dangerous.description: Risk-increasing in at least one direction. The UI must require an explicit confirmation naming old value, new value, effect and when it takes effect. UI confirmation is not security; the backend enforces regardless.

session_snapshot_value.description: For a NEXT_SESSION setting while a session is armed: the value FROZEN at arm time, which the armed session is actually bound by. Null when no session is armed or the setting is not session-snapshotted.

blockers.description: Why this setting cannot currently be changed. Empty when mutable is true.

env_var.description: The legacy/bootstrap environment variable, for provenance and an Advanced detail only. Always a variable classified as plain `config`; never a credential.

caveat.description: An operator-facing warning, such as Zerodha's whole-second book timestamps making any cross-leg exchange-dispersion limit below ~1000 ms unsatisfiable by quantisation.

updated_by.description: The operator ROLE that last changed this setting. Never a token, passcode or session identifier.
